stories.headline: BJP government passes 'Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill' in Monsoon Session of Parliament
stories.summary: The Indian Parliament has passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which extends statutory protection to the national song Vande Mataram. The bill amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, to grant Vande Mataram the same protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The legislation was passed by voice vote in the Lok Sabha, a day after it was cleared by the Rajya Sabha. Insulting Vande Mataram will now be a criminal offence, punishable with imprisonment of up to three years, a fine, or both. The bill aims to prevent insults to India's national song and promote respect for national symbols. The passage of the bill makes India's national song a protected entity, on par with the national anthem, and provides a legal framework for punishing those who insult it.

stories.summary: Indiana Senate President Pro Tem Rodric Bray faced criticism from Donald Trump after voting against a redistricting plan in December. The plan's rejection came despite intense lobbying from Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and national conservative groups. In other news, a US District Judge ruled that Trump's settlement with the IRS lacks a basis in law or fact. Additionally, prosecutors have determined that contractors, not vandals, caused damage that had been blamed on "sick" individuals, with a former Olympian previously charged. Meanwhile, Michigan's 7th District, which swung to the GOP in the 2024 election, is now the focus of a contentious Democratic primary, attracting national attention and funding. These developments highlight ongoing political tensions and controversies in the US.

stories.summary: Crosswire is a tool that allows users to compare news headlines from over 80 countries in a side-by-side layout. It provides options for comparing left, center, and right-leaning publications, and headlines can be translated into 16 languages. The platform avoids algorithmic feeds and personalization, giving users an unbiased view of the news. Similarly, Compare The News condenses front pages of 40 UK and US publications into one morning briefing, indicating each outlet's position on the political spectrum. Major US news outlets like NPR, The Washington Post, and The Guardian offer varying coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, and technology. These outlets provide in-depth coverage of major events, with options for live coverage, audio, and podcasts, allowing users to stay informed about current events from different perspectives.
